Practical life skills. Real experiences.Growing confident young people.

Across the Bridge works with children and teenagers aged about 8–16, teaching life skills the way they stick: by doing. From washing their own clothes to working outdoors and playing as a team.

Explore Our Camps Register Interest

Camps of about one week

Learning that happens with your hands

At Across the Bridge, young people aren't only taught. They take part. They try things, get them wrong, try again, and slowly discover what they're capable of.

Our programmes usually last around a week, though this can vary. Each day is built around real tasks and shared experiences, so that confidence is earned rather than lectured. The goal is simple: to help children cross the bridge from "I can't" to "I can".

Six things we help young people grow

Small daily tasks add up to big personal change.

Responsibility

Learning to take care of personal tasks and responsibilities.

Independence

Developing confidence in doing things for themselves.

Teamwork

Learning to cooperate and contribute to a group.

Discipline

Building good habits through practical activities.

Confidence

Developing confidence through participation and new experiences.

Leadership

Learning to take initiative and support others.

Our three programs

Each program supports young people alongside the people around them: family, school, church and community.

Boys aged 8–16

Boys of Honour

A boys' development and responsible-manhood program that builds identity, discipline, responsibility, leadership and readiness for the future.

  • Identity & self-worth
  • Discipline
  • Responsibility
  • Leadership
  • Future planning

Girls aged 8–16

Girls of Honour

A girls' development program that strengthens confidence, resilience, communication, leadership and readiness for the future.

  • Confidence
  • Resilience
  • Healthy relationships
  • Leadership
  • Career development

Students in partner schools

Academic Excellence

A student-success program that helps young people build learning habits, motivation and school engagement.

  • Study skills
  • Goal setting
  • Time management
  • Reading culture
  • Exam preparation

Life-skills learning

Camp ends. The growing doesn't.

Our relationship with young people doesn't stop when camp does.

Follow-up helps reinforce what children have learned and encourages continued growth once they're back home. It keeps the bridge open between the camp experience and everyday life. Change lasts best when the people around a child are part of it, so we also value working with parents, teachers and church and community leaders. Contact us to find out more about how follow-up works.

Questions parents ask

What age groups can attend?

Our camps work with children and teenagers aged approximately 8–16. Boys of Honour and Girls of Honour are designed for ages 8–16. Contact us to check the right fit for your child.

How long are the camps?

Programmes generally last around one week, although this can vary. Contact us for upcoming programme information.

What happens during camp?

Young people learn practical life skills through hands-on experiences, working both individually and as a team.

What kinds of activities do children take part in?

Washing their own clothes, outdoor work such as slashing grass, football, team activities, practical responsibilities and other life-skills activities.

Is there a girls-only camp?

Yes. Girls' Camp is a dedicated camp experience designed specifically for girls.

What happens after camp?

We continue to support young people after camp to reinforce what they learned and encourage continued growth at home, and we value involving parents and guardians. Contact us to learn more.

How can I register my child?

Fill in the interest form below, or call or WhatsApp +254 714 285 694, and we'll be in touch. Dates, fees and locations: details coming soon.
